description: Sync messages and replies from selected Slack channels. Private-channel restrictions require Enforce ACL and a successful permission read.
opening: Sync messages and replies from the public and private Slack channels you select in one workspace. Each message and each thread reply is one document, and a reply links to the message that started its thread. Shared files are downloaded and their text is searchable with the message when the download and text reading succeed.

Private-channel membership restricts search only when Enforce ACL is on and HydraDB can read the channel's members. Direct messages are not synced. Edits and deletions made in Slack after a message is synced are not picked up.

permissions.who_can_read: A public channel's messages can be read by everyone who can query the collection. A private channel's messages can be read by its members. HydraDB reads this once per channel on each sync. There is no per-message permission.
permissions.identity: A member's email address, in lower case. Bots and deactivated users have no email and are left out.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a channel's privacy, members or member emails, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: A private channel with more than 1,000 members who have emails, or more than 3,000 members in all, cannot be captured. Set an access rule on such a channel.
Without `users:read.email`, permissions cannot be captured for any private channel.

connect.auth: Slack uses a token from a Slack app installed in your workspace. A bot token or a user token works.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A Slack bot token, which starts with `xoxb-`, or a user token, which starts with `xoxp-`.

connect.permissions_label: Scopes to add to the Slack app

permissions.name: channels:read
permissions.text: lists public channels for you to select.

permissions.name: groups:read
permissions.text: lists private channels for you to select.

permissions.name: users:read.email
permissions.text: without it, permissions cannot be captured for any private channel.

connect.permissions_note: If neither `channels:read` nor `groups:read` is granted, connecting fails with a message that names the missing scope.

steps.title: Create a Slack app
steps.text: Create a Slack app for your workspace and add the scopes above.

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: Install the app in the workspace and copy its token.

steps.title: Select channels
steps.text: HydraDB lists the non-archived channels the token can see. For each channel, it shows privacy, app membership and member count. Select the channels to sync.

connect.account: One token covers one Slack workspace.

sync.first_sync: A newly selected channel reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: New messages and replies are synced from recent history. New replies on older threads are checked every 6 hours by default. That check covers channel history over multiple syncs, so older replies may arrive later.
sync.edits: A routine sync does not pick up an edit to a message that is already synced.
sync.deletes: Deleted messages are not removed. A message deleted in Slack stays searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Messages
documents.one_document: One Slack message: a message posted in a channel, or a single reply in a thread.
documents.title: The channel name with `#`, a colon and the message's first line, cut to about 80 characters, for example `#general: Deploy is done`. A reply reads `#general thread: ...`. A message with no text is titled `Slack message`. When a message has text, search matches the message, not this title, so a channel name in a query does not reliably limit results to that channel.
documents.text: The message text, with mentions turned into display names. Then the pretext, title and text of any legacy attachments, and one `[file: name]` line per shared file. The sender is written as a `From` line and the time as a `Sent` line.
documents.link_back: A Slack permalink to the message. A reply links to itself inside its thread. Empty if the workspace address could not be read.
documents.files: Each shared file is downloaded and read, and its text becomes searchable with the message. A file is skipped if Slack gave no download address, the download fails, or the file is too large.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The display name of the person or bot that posted, written as the `From` line. The graph records the message as sent by that person. If the name could not be read, the raw Slack id is kept, and later syncs do not go back to fix it.

attributes.name: Shared files
attributes.text: The text read from each shared file, searchable with the message.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: The message time, written as the `Sent` line.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Display names of people mentioned in the message. The graph records each as mentioned.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_ts
attributes.text: The message's Slack timestamp. Picks out one exact message. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_thread_ts
attributes.text: The timestamp of the thread's first message, empty outside a thread. Limits a query to one thread. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_subtype
attributes.text: Slack's message subtype, such as `bot_message` or `file_share`. Includes or excludes bot posts and file shares. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_bot_id
attributes.text: The bot id when a bot posted the message. Includes or excludes one bot's messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_reply_count
attributes.text: How many replies the thread has. Finds thread starters by how many replies they drew. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `slack`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a reply, the message that started its thread. Joins the reply to that message, so the whole conversation can be returned together. Not searchable.

attributes.name: thread_id
attributes.text: The thread a message belongs to. Groups every message of one thread together in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Channel
attributes.text: The selected channel. For a private channel, its members decide who can read its messages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: attachment_count
attributes.text: How many legacy attachments the message had.

attributes.name: file_count
attributes.text: How many shared files Slack listed, including any that could not be downloaded.

attributes.name: is_edited
attributes.text: Whether Slack marked the message as edited when it was read. Later edits are not picked up automatically.

attributes.name: edited_by
attributes.text: The display name of the editor, when edited. The editor is not added to the graph as a person.

attributes.name: edited_at
attributes.text: The edit time, when edited. The result date stays the original message time.

attributes.name: slack_files
attributes.text: The details Slack supplied for each shared file, kept even when a file's text could not be read.

example_searches: What did the team decide about the release last week?
What did Priya say in the thread about the pricing change?
Which messages were posted by the alerts bot?

connections: A thread reply to the message that started the thread.
Every message to its thread, including a message nobody replied to.
No links to items in other tools.
people: An editor is kept with the message but not added to the graph.
graph.from_text: The message text, legacy attachment text and shared file text. Each reply is read together with the text of its thread's first message.

not_synced: Archived channels: HydraDB does not list them for selection.
Direct messages and group direct messages.
System messages: joins, leaves, renames, topic and purpose changes, pins, bots being added or removed, and thread broadcasts.
Edits and deletions made after a message was synced.
